key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines weld-pool simulation, AI surrogates, and robotic control to screen in-space welding conditions before physical testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support robotic welding control for on-orbit assembly and repair, while reducing reliance on scarce flight-like tests.
method: Finite-volume thermal model with phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates evaluated using repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated six-axis robot with proportional power-setting control along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; 74/80 held-out solver responses fell within nominal 90% predictive intervals, and closed-loop simulation met the illustrative width band at 12/12 points versus 9/12 open-loop.
watch_item: Results remain simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop tests are needed to assess model and controller validity.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
